correctness.rationale: The six possible four-seat compositions split into four classes; the dominated class is eliminated algebraically, and exact differences show the PAV transition at 4/3. Full greedy marginal comparisons, including equality cases, place its transition at 3/2. Thus all greedy paths fail exactly for \(4/3<y/x<3/2\) with gap \((3y-4x)/12\). A pair of independent exact implementations (aggregated and six labeled candidates) enumerate all 147 sorted positive integer triples through 17 voters, including 123 with fewer than 17, proving restricted-domain minimality. The actual packaged verifier is replayed; finite tests do not substitute for the real-parameter proof.

originality.rationale: The result is the complete tie-break-independent PAV/seq-PAV phase boundary, exact loss, and sharp minimum electorate on a fixed three-bloc, six-candidate, four-seat triangle domain. The general phenomenon seq-PAV != PAV is prior work: Example 2.5 in Lackner–Skowron gives a two-seat discrepancy with five ballot types. Dong–Lederer studies axiomatic characterizations; the inspected party-approval manuscript studies incentive and representation axioms. Their statements do not imply these exact composition-phase thresholds or the 17-voter restricted-domain cutoff. Actual semantic and scientific-source searches found no stronger covering theorem; remaining publication-priority uncertainty is recorded. Janson (2016) documents earlier optimization–addition discrepancies with two seats, explicitly credited; its inspected results do not give the restricted triangle characterization.
residual_risks: A mathematically equivalent exact triangle/capacity-two comparison could appear in specialist reports or unindexed sources beyond those inspected.
General candidate-clone and party-apportionment results may contain an unrecognized specialized corollary; explicit relevant theorems located to date do not.
The finite enumeration certifies only the specified domain, not a global minimum across unrestricted approval profiles.

value.rationale: The three pairwise-overlapping approval blocs form a minimal cyclic coalition structure of real social-choice interest; the theorem identifies two distinct rational transition ratios, a robust interval immune to tie-breaking, an exact welfare loss and a sharp first electorate for the unrestricted three-weight version of the same finite triangle domain. These are actionable structural benchmarks for comparing harmonic greedy allocation with global committee optimization rather than a textbook deduction or an arbitrary unmotivated numerical slice.
